extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale, publicly available benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification (RESISC), containing 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images per class. It features big variations in translation, spatial resolution, viewpoint, object pose, illumination, background, and occlusion, and has high within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.citeAs: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu, 'Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art', Proceedings of the IEEE, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted from Google Earth by experts in remote sensing image interpretation. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales, covering more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were extracted from Google Earth, which maps the Earth by superimposing images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were cropped to a size of 256×256 pixels in RGB color space. The spatial resolution varies from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel for most scene classes, except for island, lake, mountain, and snowberg which have lower spatial resolutions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets and searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar to form 45 meaningful scene classes. Each image is labeled with one of these scene classes.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables the development and evaluation of data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification, which has applications in natural hazards detection, land use determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes images from over 100 countries and regions, covering developing, transition, and highly developed economies, but specific biases are not discussed.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that existing datasets (including this one) rely only on traditional remote sensing (overhead imagery) and suggests future work could combine remote sensing data with social media and spatial technology for improved classification.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is used for benchmarking state-of-the-art scene classification methods, including handcrafted features, unsupervised feature learning, and deep learning-based methods. Experimental setups include 10%-90% and 20%-80% training-test splits.
